children: Adani Enterprises shares rose in morning trade on Wednesday, bucking weak broader markets, after its airport subsidiary signed a shareholders’ agreement with a clutch of marquee global investors to raise funds. The investors include BlackRock, Temasek, Premji Invest and Alpha Wave, for the sale of up to a 5.54 percent stake.

The Adani Enterprises stock was up 1.45 percent at Rs 2,996 in morning trade, beating a sharp decline in the broader market. At 9:25 am, the Sensex was down 516 points, or 0.68 percent, at 75,061.90, while the Nifty 50 declined 0.51 percent to 23,513.40.

Adani Enterprises shares have gained around 32.5 percent so far in 2026, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen about 10 percent over the same period. The flagship Adani Group company's market capitalisation stood at around Rs 4.05 lakh crore.

In a regulatory filing on September 9, Adani Enterprises said it had entered into a shareholders’ agreement with wholly owned subsidiary Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL) and identified investors for raising funds through the issuance of equity shares by AAHL. The investors will acquire a stake of up to 5.54 percent in the airport operator.

The identified investors include Alpha Wave III, Premji Invest and Temasek's Jongsong Investments, along with four BlackRock funds -- BlackRock Global Allocation Portfolio, BlackRock Global Funds - Global Allocation Fund, BlackRock Strategic Income Opportunities Portfolio and BlackRock Global Funds - Fixed Income Global Opportunities Fund.

The development marks a significant step forward in AAHL's fund-raising exercise. Moneycontrol had reported exclusively last week that BlackRock was exploring a significant equity infusion into the airport operator as part of a proposed transaction that could value AAHL at more than $20 billion. At the time, discussions were said to be at an advanced stage, but BlackRock had yet to take a final decision.

Wednesday's filing confirms BlackRock's participation in the shareholders’ agreement, alongside the other investors, although Adani Enterprises did not disclose the size of the fund raise, the issue price or the valuation at which the shares would be issued.

Adani Enterprises currently owns 100 percent of AAHL. The rights under the shareholders’ agreement will become effective after the first tranche of investment by the identified investors is completed and will subsequently be incorporated into AAHL's Articles of Association.

AAHL will issue new equity shares representing up to 5.54 percent of its equity capital to the investors, meaning the transaction involves a primary capital infusion into the airport company rather than Adani Enterprises selling its existing shares.

AAHL is India's largest private-sector airport operator. As of FY26, it managed nearly 23 percent of India's passenger traffic and 29 percent of its air cargo. Its portfolio includes airports in Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Mangaluru, Jaipur, Guwahati and Thiruvananthapuram, besides the Navi Mumbai airport project.
